title: Looking for playtesters: Neon Kamikaze GP, an anti-grav racing management game (Windows, free)
author: OCompany
selftext:
Hi all. My game is ready for its first outside playtest. I'm looking for a handful of people to play it and tell me what breaks, anything confusing, is it fun, balance concerns, etc.  All the hits, all the good ones.

**\*\*What it is\*\***

Neon Kamikaze GP is a racing management game set in a neon Tokyo. You run a small garage in a six-team league. You don't drive. You buy and repair parts, choose who races, and give your driver orders during the race: CONSERVE, MAINTAIN, PUSH, ATTACK, DEFEND, or KAMIKAZE, which is fast and can make your car explode. When a part starts failing mid-race, the race slows down and you decide what to do. After each race, a report shows what ended your race and why.

Drivers age, improve, retire, and can be hurt or killed. A season is six rounds across three circuits, and there's a weekly parts market where your Engineer tells you whether a part is worth buying.

**\*\*How it was made\*\***

With AI throughout, and I'm happy to talk about the workflow in the comments. Claude wrote much of the code under my direction, and the portraits and backgrounds were made with image models (Seedream and GPT Image). The design, the systems, the balance and the music are mine. Built in Godot 4.

**\*\*What I'm asking\*\***

\- Start a new career and keep the Engineer's guide on.

\- Play as long as you like. Even one race week helps.

\- Tell me anything that broke, looked wrong, or that you couldn't work out, and what you did just before. Screenshots help a lot.

Nothing is timed or scored. I'm testing the game, not testing you.

**\*\*The build\*\***

Windows only. It's a ZIP: unzip it and run the .exe. There's no installer. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the file isn't signed yet (click "More info", then "Run anyway"). The game saves by itself.

**\*\*How to get it\*\***

Send me a message and I'll reply with a Google Drive link to the ZIP.

Thanks for reading!
